references.text: The original command from God to Moses to make four gold rings for the table, which Exodus 37:13 fulfills.
A parallel command for four gold rings that were to be attached at the four corners by the feet of the table.
The same chapter describes similar casting of gold rings for the ark of the covenant, showing the craftsmanship technique of casting rings and attaching them.
Describes the placement of the rings near the rim as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
Shows the use of gold for rings in the construction of the tabernacle, following the same craft tradition.
Both the table and the bronze altar share the same structural solution with four rings at the corners for carrying poles.
Both objects (the table and the altar) have rings for carrying poles, emphasizing that the entire worship system was portable.
